name: Samuel Tak Lee
profile: Hong Kong property magnate (Prudential Enterprises; owner of London's Langham Estate in Fitzrovia). Died at his London home on 24 May 2026, aged 87, per The Telegraph (cited on Wikipedia).
notes: Deceased 24 May 2026. Sources: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2026/05/24/west-ends-billionaire-hong-kong-landlord-dies/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Tak_Lee. Langham Estate/Prudential Enterprises now with family/heirs.

name: Robert E "Ted" Turner
profile: Founder of CNN, TBS, TNT and Turner Broadcasting; philanthropist (UN Foundation, Nuclear Threat Initiative). Died 6 May 2026 aged 87, announced by Turner Enterprises.
notes: Deceased 6 May 2026. Source: https://www.wlox.com/2026/05/06/ted-turner-cnn-founder-cable-news-pioneer-dies-87/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Turner

name: Maurice Greenberg
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Starr Companies (C.V. Starr & Co.); sons Jeff and Scott Greenberg took over leadership in 2025
profile: Maurice 'Hank' Greenberg (b. 1925) ran AIG from 1968 to 2005, building it into one of the world's largest insurers, then led C.V. Starr & Co. (Starr Companies), a global insurance and investment group. In 2025 he handed leadership to his sons and he chaired The Starr Foundation until 2024; he remains active in US-China and medical philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A WWII veteran, he enlisted at 17, landed at Omaha Beach on D-Day and took part in the liberation of Dachau; he later served in Korea, and credits the GI Bill for his college education.
deep_cut_fact: In 1990 he became the first Chairman of Shanghai's International Business Leaders' Advisory Council, later served as Senior Economic Advisor to the Beijing municipal government, and was made an honorary citizen of Shanghai.

public_contacts.value: Prosek Partners (listed as Starr's PR adviser, Oct 2025 release)

notes: Aged 101; Hurun-listed wealth via Starr. Best route is Starr media office (media@starr.com). Starr Foundation does not accept unsolicited proposals.

name: Sanjiv Goenka
profile: Sanjiv Goenka chairs the ~$4.9bn-revenue RPSG Group, formed in 2011 when his father RP Goenka's empire was split between him and brother Harsh. Flagship is 127-year-old Kolkata power utility CESC, alongside PCBL, Spencer's, Too Yumm! and sports (Lucknow Super Giants, Mohun Bagan, Manchester Originals). In 2026 the group announced Rs 15,800 crore capex in West Bengal across energy and more.
interesting_fact: His older brother Harsh Goenka, who runs the separate RPG Enterprises, is also a billionaire; in 2025 Sanjiv bought 70% of English cricket team Manchester Originals.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired IIT Kharagpur's Board of Governors since 2002, nominated for a fifth time in 2021, and was CII president in 2001-02 at about 40.
notes: Energy angle is strong (CESC power utility; son Shashwat, vice chairman, pushing renewables). The @RP_SanjivGoenka X link appears on the group homepage. CII term: https://cii.in/CII_Past_presidents.aspx

name: Lorenzo Fertitta
current_role: Vice Chairman/director, Red Rock Resorts (Station Casinos); Chairman, Fertitta Capital
profile: Las Vegas-born Lorenzo Fertitta and brother Frank bought the near-bankrupt UFC for $2m in 2001; he served as its chairman/CEO and they sold to WME-IMG in 2016 at a $4bn valuation. He remains vice chairman of Red Rock Resorts, the locals-casino company founded by their father, and chairs Fertitta Capital, the family's venture/growth investment firm launched in 2017.
interesting_fact: The brothers got hooked on martial arts taking weekly lessons in their casino's basement; they bought UFC for $2m in 2001 and exited at roughly $4-5bn valuations in 2016-17.
deep_cut_fact: Before owning UFC he was a regulator of it: he sat on the Nevada State Athletic Commission from 1996 until July 2000, when he left to become president of Station Casinos. He also holds an MBA from NYU Stern, where he later funded veterans' scholarships.
notes: Fertitta Capital site had no published contact. Childhood friend of Dana White. Not to be confused with cousin Tilman Fertitta.

name: Ren Yuanlin
current_role: Founder/honorary chairman, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (son Ren Letian is executive chairman since 2020); controller of Shanshan Co. via investment platform
profile: Ren Yuanlin turned a failing state-owned Jiangyin yard into Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, one of China's largest and most profitable shipbuilders (SGX-listed). He handed the chair to son Ren Letian in 2020; in 2022 Yangzijiang Financial was spun off. In 2025 a Ren-led consortium took control of Ningbo Shanshan, the world's largest lithium-battery anode supplier, in a court-led restructuring.
interesting_fact: In late 2025 the shipping tycoon moved into EV batteries: his consortium paid about RMB 3.2bn for ~23% control of Shanshan, which holds roughly 21% of the global anode-material market, making Ren its actual controller.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the yard (then Jiangyin Shipbuilding Factory) in the 1970s as a young technician, ran its ship-body (hull) workshop, rose to factory supervisor and became chairman in 1997.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. Strong energy/battery angle via Shanshan. Separate entity Yangzijiang Maritime Development (public@yzjmaritime.com, per search result only) is not the shipbuilder. SGX filing on Shanshan: https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/J4HMJ4YW8Z36QGX3/2a2655ec83d9aa4d67ba46901f928072638151dc862fbdce983b03daa9c28c51

name: Jamie Dimon
profile: Jamie Dimon has run JPMorgan Chase, the largest US bank by assets, as CEO since 2005-06 and chairman since 2006-07, after helping Sandy Weill build Citigroup and leading Bank One. His stake and pay make him one of few bank-CEO billionaires. In June 2026 JPMorgan named Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh co-presidents; Dimon reportedly plans about three more years as CEO before becoming executive chairman.
interesting_fact: His Greek grandfather, a banker in Smyrna and Athens, changed the family name from Papademetriou to Dimon; his father and grandfather were both stockbrokers at Shearson.
deep_cut_fact: His break came from a college paper: at Tufts he wrote about Shearson's mergers, his mother sent it to Sandy Weill, and Weill hired him for a summer job doing budgets at Shearson.

public_contacts.value: Global Communications: Joe Evangelisti (no email listed); IR/HR media: michael.f.fusco@jpmchase.com

notes: Go through JPMorgan Global Communications. He publishes an annual shareholder letter, which is a good hook for outreach. Succession source: https://www.foxbusiness.com/business-leaders/jpmorgan-names-2-new-co-presidents-setting-up-race-succeed-jamie-dimon

name: Do Won Chang
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO, Forever 21 (no current role found)
profile: Korean-born Do Won Chang emigrated to Los Angeles in 1981 and in 1984 co-founded Forever 21 with his wife Jin Sook, growing it from one 900 sq ft store to roughly 800 stores worldwide. The family-owned chain filed for bankruptcy in 2019 and its assets were sold in 2020; Forbes no longer lists the Changs as billionaires. No public information found on his activities since.
interesting_fact: The couple started the first store, Fashion 21 in Highland Park, LA, with $11,000 in savings and reached $700,000 in first-year sales, then opened a new store roughly every six months.
deep_cut_fact: Carnegie Corporation of New York named him one of its 'Great Immigrants' in 2017. Forever 21 bags carried 'John 3:16' printed on the bottom, reflecting the founders' Christian faith.
notes: No longer a billionaire after the 2019 bankruptcy; Forbes/Hurun listings are stale (2011-2019). Very private, with no published contact channel. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (born 1954; no death reported). Shares listing with wife Jin Sook Chang.

name: Jenny Love
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Culture Officer, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores
profile: Jenny Love Meyer is the daughter of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Oklahoma City-based Love's Travel Stops in 1964; the family-owned chain now runs 670+ travel stops and convenience stores in 42 states. She joined in 1991, spent about two decades as VP of communications and since 2019 has been EVP and chief culture officer, overseeing culture, PR, community relations and giving. Hurun lists her among the family's billionaires.
interesting_fact: Love's, a family-owned fuel retailer with nearly 40,000 team members, has an alternative-energy arm building EV charging and other alt-fuel offerings at its truck stops.
deep_cut_fact: She has a political science BA from Colorado College, and under her leadership Love's has donated more than $60 million to Children's Miracle Network Hospitals, on whose board of trustees she sits.

public_contacts.value: lauren.daniels@loves.com (Love's media relations specialist, per 2025 releases)

notes: Hurun lists her as 'Jenny Love'; she is publicly known as Jenny Love Meyer. As CCO she oversees PR herself, so Love's communications team is the natural route. Mother Judy Love died Nov 2024. Energy angle via Love's alt-fuel/EV build-out. Appointment release: https://www.loves.com/news/2019/november/loves-announces-jenny-love-meyer-as-chief-culture-officer

name: Glen Taylor
current_role: Chairman, Taylor Corp. (North Mankato, MN); owner of the Minneapolis Star Tribune
profile: Glen Taylor bought a wedding-invitation printer for $2m in 1975 (where he had worked through college) and built it into Taylor Corp., a printing and marketing firm with over $2bn in sales. He owned the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx from 1994 until the $1.5bn sale to Marc Lore and Alex Rodriguez closed in 2025. He still owns the Star Tribune and Midwest farmland, and is now giving farmland away to rural causes.
interesting_fact: Before he was a sports owner he was a politician: a Republican Minnesota state senator from 1981 to 1990, serving as Senate Minority Leader in the mid-1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Raised on a 150-acre farm near Comfrey, MN (corn, soybeans, flax, dairy cows), he set up the Taylor Family Farms Foundation in 2023 with ~$172m of farmland and added another $100m+ in Jan 2026. Farmers keep working the land and the rent funds rural grants in southern MN and northwest Iowa.
notes: Farm-upbringing source: https://www.startribune.com/from-farm-boy-to-billionaire-glen-taylor-steers-his-own-course/265057261. Timberwolves sale: https://www.fox9.com/news/timberwolves-sale-approved-nba-governors-june-2025. Taylor Family Farms Foundation may be a softer route for outreach.

name: Peter Unger
current_role: Private investor via Unger family office (Unger Capital Management), Weiden, Bavaria
profile: Peter Unger founded Auto-Teile-Unger (A.T.U.) in 1985 and built it into Germany's largest auto parts and repair chain. He sold 72% to Doughty Hanson in 2002 for $900m and the rest to KKR in 2004 for $360m (A.T.U. is now owned by France's Mobivia). He now invests through a Weiden-based family office in listed stocks, startups and German residential and commercial real estate, including thousands of Berlin apartments with Groth Gruppe.
interesting_fact: In Berlin he has bought or co-financed the construction of thousands of apartments with developer Groth Gruppe; his other bets include e-bike and sensor-tech startups.
deep_cut_fact: A.T.U. grew fast: after the 1985 start it opened a branch in Aschaffenburg in 1986 and its 100th branch, in Kulmbach, in 1992, seven years after founding.
notes: Very private. No published contact; family office is Unger Capital Management, Weiden (per altss.com profile, not an official site). Do not confuse with the NYU philosopher Peter Unger. Alive status not confirmed by a recent source, though he is still on Forbes real-time 2026.

name: Tao Meiying
current_role: Co-owner (with husband Zhang Jun) of Funde Holdings / Funde Sino Life Insurance (富德生命人寿); no current executive title found
profile: Tao Meiying (陶美萦) is the wife of Zhang Jun, founder and controller of Shenzhen-based Funde Holdings (富德控股), parent of Funde Sino Life Insurance and other insurance and asset-management units. Hurun lists the couple jointly. She was general manager and executive director of Funde Group until Zhang took over those posts in Dec 2022 and Feb 2023.
interesting_fact: Funde Sino Life has been named to the Asia's 500 Brands list fifteen times, per a Sept 2026 Xinhua report.
notes: Very low public profile and no English-language coverage. Wealth is via husband Zhang Jun's Funde group; outreach would go through Funde corporate communications. Role-change source: https://www.36kr.com/p/2873126518493568. Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Phillip Ruffin
current_role: Owner, Treasure Island (TI) and Circus Circus, Las Vegas; Ruffin Companies (Wichita)
profile: Wichita-raised Phil Ruffin built a fortune in Midwest convenience stores, then hotels, oil distribution and hand-truck manufacturing before moving into casinos. He bought the New Frontier (and ended a record strike), sold the site for about $1.2bn in 2007, then bought Treasure Island from MGM in 2009 (~$775m) and Circus Circus in 2019-20 ($825m). Forbes ranked him No. 972 in 2026 at about $4.3bn.
interesting_fact: In 1972 he pioneered self-serve gasoline in Kansas, building a chain of about 60 Midwest convenience stores whose cash funded his first hotel, a Wichita Marriott, in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: He was a state wrestling champion at Wichita North High School (class of 1953). One profile recalls that his father, who never went to a match, asked whether he was the one the newspaper was talking about. His family's surname was originally 'Rufan'.
notes: Aged about 90-91. Long-time Trump friend. Recent profile: https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/for-phil-ruffin-timing-is-everything. Has floated selling Circus Circus at ~$5bn (Forbes, Jan 2025). No dedicated press email found.

name: Guenther Lehmann
current_role: Former co-owner of dm-drogerie markt; stake transferred to his son in 2016; reportedly moved to dm's supervisory board; managing director of Günther Lehmann GmbH & Co. KG, Karlsruhe (per marketscreener)
profile: Guenther Lehmann, then running his family's Karlsruhe grocery chain Pfannkuch, invested in Götz Werner's young drugstore chain dm in November 1974 and received 50% of the company. dm became Germany's leading drugstore chain (~$12bn revenue). Lehmann was never involved operationally, and in 2016 he transferred his dm stake to his son, so he dropped off Forbes after 2021.
interesting_fact: dm is half-owned by a charitable foundation: founder Götz Werner moved his 50% into a foundation, and his son Christoph Werner runs the company. dm's employee-first philosophy is well known in German-speaking countries.
deep_cut_fact: He came in as the 'junior heir' of Karlsruhe grocery chain Pfannkuch, investing in dm in 1974, a year after Werner opened the first store in Karlsruhe in 1973.
notes: Extremely private, with no public statements or channels. Wealth now largely sits with his son as a dm limited partner, and listings after 2021 are stale. Succession source: https://www.lebensmittelzeitung.net/handel/nachrichten/Anteile-uebertragen-dm-Mitgesellschafter-Lehman-hat-Nachfolge-geregelt-131003. No death report found.

current_role: Listed by Hurun as linked to 'Jimei Technology' (electrical equipment), jointly with Fang Junyun; role not verified
profile: Hurun China and Global lists (2017-2026) include Fang Jining (方骥柠), jointly with Fang Junyun, with wealth from 'Jimei Technology' in electrical equipment (about $2.3bn). name: Cai Jianyong
current_role: Chairman and Executive Director (also General Manager/CEO), Lygend Resources & Technology (HKEX: 2245), Ningbo
profile: Cai Jianyong founded Ningbo-based Lygend in 2009 after nearly a decade in commodities trading, and built it into a nickel supplier spanning ore trading and smelting. With Indonesian partner Harita it runs HPAL and RKEF smelters on Obi Island that make battery-grade nickel for EVs. Lygend listed in Hong Kong in Nov 2022; 2025 revenue rose 37.7% to RMB 40.2bn.
interesting_fact: Lygend's Obi Island HPAL plant was among the first in Indonesia to ship EV-battery-grade nickel sulfate, and in Jan 2026 it formed a JV to build an HPAL slag-treatment plant on the island.
deep_cut_fact: A Shanghai Institute of Building Materials Industry graduate, he closed his ESG-report chairman's letter with the line that Lygend would use 'responsibility as our vessel and innovation as our paddle' to navigate the global tide of sustainable development.
notes: Strong energy/battery-materials angle (Indonesian nickel for EV batteries). Low personal media profile. 2025 results: https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0331/2026033104229.pdf

name: Wang Xinwen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Lilith Games (莉莉丝), Shanghai
profile: Wang Xinwen (Kenny Wang) co-founded Shanghai's Lilith Games in 2013 with former classmates Yuan Shuai and Zhang Hao after about three years at Tencent. Lilith became one of China's most successful global mobile-game makers with Rise of Kingdoms (2018), AFK Arena and AFK Journey, and runs the publishing brand Farlight Games. He appears on Hurun's under-40 and unicorn-founder lists.
interesting_fact: Asked whether Lilith was 'China's Supercell', he replied: 'No, we don't want to be China's Supercell, we want to be Lilith of the world.'
deep_cut_fact: Lilith started with just RMB 2 million of backing when the three Tencent colleagues quit to make mobile instead of PC games; Wang is a Nanjing University graduate.
notes: Known in English as Kenny Wang. Video profile with links to his talks: https://kaleland.substack.com/p/video-who-is-wang-xinwen-lilith-games. Education per marketscreener (secondary source). No dedicated press email found.

name: Mario Gabelli
current_role: Founder & Chairman, GAMCO Investors (Gabelli Funds, OTCQX: GAMI); Executive Chairman, Associated Capital Group
profile: Bronx-born Mario Gabelli founded Gabelli/GAMCO in 1977 and became one of Wall Street's best-known value investors, making his name on media and telecom stocks in the 1980s. GAMCO, now Palm Beach-based, manages about $35bn. He is executive chairman of spin-off Associated Capital, a Giving Pledge signatory, and the namesake of Fordham's Gabelli School of Business.
interesting_fact: A lifelong contrarian: around age five he set up a shoe-shine box at a Bronx subway station, and he bought his first stocks at 13.
deep_cut_fact: His interest in stocks began on the golf course: as a boy he hitchhiked from the Bronx to Westchester to caddie for NYSE floor specialists, listened to their market talk, and later used a caddie scholarship toward his Fordham tuition.

public_contacts.value: jsalata@gabelli.com (Jason Salata, contact on March 2026 firm update)

notes: GAMCO said in March 2026 that he had stepped back from day-to-day duties; Chris Marangi was named GAMCO President in March and joined the board in Sept 2026. Check his current availability before outreach. No death reported. Other press releases list CLO David Goldman or CAO Kieran Caterina as contacts.

name: Luis Riu
current_role: CEO (sole CEO since 2024), RIU Hotels & Resorts, Palma de Mallorca
profile: Luis Riu Güell (b. 1960, Palma) is the third generation of the Mallorca hotel family that started with an 80-bed hotel on Playa de Palma in 1953. He co-led RIU with his sister Carmen from 1998 and became sole CEO after her 2024 retirement. RIU runs about 100 hotels in 22 countries (6.8m guests in 2025, $4.5bn+ revenue), and his sons Luis and Roberto Riu Rodríguez are taking on growing roles.
interesting_fact: He is said to personally scout and approve every international resort location before construction, and he drove RIU's 2010 entry into New York's Times Square with its first urban 'Riu Plaza' city hotels.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Barcelona business graduate who started as a hotel director and head of expansion in the Canary Islands, he is known in-house for his passion for architecture and hotel design; he is personally involved in every phase of new builds and writes personal posts on the RIU blog.
notes: Forbes still calls him co-CEO with sister Carmen, but per RIU she retired in 2024. Succession coverage: https://www.riu.com/en/news/generational-handover-luis-roberto-riu. Commenting on one of his blog posts is a natural outreach hook.

name: Gunther Lehner
current_role: Family owner and former CEO (1997-2021) of ALPLA Group, Hard, Austria; son Philipp Lehner is CEO since 2021
profile: Günther Lehner is the second-generation owner of ALPLA, the Vorarlberg plastic-packaging maker his father Alwin and uncle Helmuth founded in 1955. He took over management in 1997 and built ALPLA into one of the world's largest rigid-packaging makers (bottles, caps, preforms), with ~206 plants in 45 countries and €5.2bn sales in 2025. He handed the CEO role to son Philipp in 2021.
interesting_fact: ALPLA began in 1955 as a start-up in a laundry room (Waschküche) in Hard; in 1958 the brothers built the Alplamat, the first extrusion blow-moulding machine for plastic bottles.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s he pushed ALPLA into recycling, turning it into a 'system provider'. ALPLA has run PET recycling since taking majority control of Austria's PET Recycling Team in 2010 and now operates rPET/rHDPE plants in about 10 countries.

public_contacts.value: erik.nielsen@alpla.com (Erik Nielsen, Team Leader Corporate Communications, ALPLA)

notes: Low public profile; CEO Philipp Lehner is now the public face. No death reported, but no recent appearance confirmed either. FY2025 results: https://blog.alpla.com/en/press-release/newsroom/stable-financial-year-2025-alpla-achieves-turnover-eu52-billion
